messages:
takashi: quick heads-up — bringing Origami-v1 (int4) canary up on us-west-2. smoke looks ok for en/ja, but when we feed mixed CJK + RTL (arabic fragments) we see bracket orientation flips and an extra token inserted before closing brackets. BLEU drops ~4.3 pts vs float baseline on our multilingual devset.

liang: can you paste a minimal repro sample?

takashi: sure — running locally with the same model bundle+tokenizer: 
```bash
# run canary eval (shortened)
python eval.py --model origami-v1-int4 --dataset multilingual-mixctx --subset quick-smoke --output out.json
```
example input: "中文(العربية) test"
expected detok: "中文(العربية) test"
actual detok: "中文( العربية ) test"  <-- extra space and bracket mirrored on the RTL side
metrics snippet:
- BLEU: float 28.4 -> int4 24.1
- chrF: float 55.2 -> int4 50.9
- token counts: float 8 -> int4 10 (2 extra tokens around parens)

maria: wow. could be tokenizer normalization mismatch or quant kernel shuffling token ids. did we pin tokenizers? which tokenizer version in the bundle?

takashi: bundle lists tokenizer v2026-02-10 (same as float run), but the runtime path loads native tokenizers from wheel built in CI (we upgraded sentencepiece yesterday). suspect mismatch between model->vocab mapping and runtime tokenization post-quantize kernel mapping.

svetlana: also check Unicode normalization (NFC vs NFKC) and zero-width joiner handling. mixed CJK+RTL often exposes ZWNJ/ZWJ edgecases. Could be the detok code doing a bidi reflow after token-level whitespace ops.

liang: @takashi can you dump the raw token ids (float vs int4) for that sample? quick diff might show where split happens.

takashi: posted diffs to the thread file (shortened):
```
# float ids: [102, 3456, 12, 78, 223, 90]
# int4 ids:   [102, 3456, 12, 4001, 78, 223, 90]  # inserted 4001 (" ") before paren-close
```
looks like an extra space token sneaks in before closing bracket only in int4 path.

eval-bot: automated eval summary for 1763801234: BLEU_delta=-4.3, chrF_delta=-4.3, token_delta=+2, failing_locales=[zh-ar, ja-ar]. See /internal/evals/1763801234 for full output. :chart_with_downwards_trend:

maria: two immediate hypotheses: (1) quant-residual rounding introduced new id remap in embedding/table lookup when id collision occurs, (2) tokenization pipeline mismatch (sentencepiece compile flags) between float and quant bundles.

svetlana: action items I propose:
- dump tokenizer logits->ids path for the sample (takashi)
- run tiny bisect: quantize only weights vs quantize weights+embeddings to isolate embedding remap
- run detokenizer with bidi-debug on (print grapheme clusters and normalization step)
- run same canary with runtime pinned to older sentencepiece wheel (2026-02-03)

liang: I'll kick off the two bisect jobs (weights-only / weights+emb) on canary compute now, tagging results into the eval job.

takashi: thanks. I'll add a small repro harness that prints token ids + grapheme boundaries and post to the internal gist. if we confirm embedding id remap, we need an urgent rollback of the quantized embedding packaging.

maria: also add a small targeted eval for bracket-heavy CJK+RTL pairs across locales so we can set a guardrail for rollout (blocker if BLEU delta > 2.0 in zh-ar/en-ar mixes).

takashi: noted. i'll block the canary promotion until we either fix or add fallback routing to float model for affected locales.

svetlana: fyi we've seen similar ZWJ/ZWNJ token splits with QAT in another family last quarter — ping me if you want the old bisect script.

liang: job updates: bisect-weights-only queued (job 6723), bisect-embeddings queued (job 6724). will post artifacts when done.

takashi: thanks team. keeping thread updated. :eyes:
